reviews.body: I have been using Dr. Sheth’s Haldi & Hyaluronic Acid Sunscreen for the past 3 years and was very satisfied with the 50g version. Recently, I purchased the 80g pack, and I noticed a significant difference in the formula. The earlier 50g tube had a light yellow tint (which I assume is due to haldi), and the texture was balanced and suitable for my skin. However, the new 80g pack does not have the same light yellow color. It appears more white, and the texture feels noticeably more oily. To compare properly, I applied the old sunscreen on the left side of my face and the new one on the right side. The difference was clearly visible — the right side (new pack) looked much more oily and shiny. As a long-term user, this change is disappointing because the previous formula suited my skin very well. I hope the brand maintains consistency in their formulation across different pack sizes.

reviews.author: Meghali Ghosh

reviews.title: Great for oily skin
reviews.body: My skin is extremely oily, and I've tried several pricey sunscreens, including those from foreign companies, but they all irritate my eyes, leave me with a horrible white cast, and leave white lines around my cheeks and eye lids after a few hours. Applying this sunscreen on top of the ceramide and vitamin C moisturizing cream is like magic. In contrast to other sunscreens, it mixes in seconds. I don't think it looks or feels like anything on my face. I also think that the niacinamide in this sunscreen is effective because, even after using it for a few weeks, the texture of my skin has changed noticeably. Dietsabya ki jai ho 🙌
